title: fix(service-automation): reach a nested run's whole chain from the operator exit
body:
Fixes #15222

Clause-②: yes

## The condition this is an exit from

`resumeInternal`'s catch arm journalled the consumed suspension of THE RUN THAT THREW, and nothing else. For a nested run the ancestors were handled on both paths with no journal at all:

- **up-bubble** (`skipBubble === false`): `failAncestors` walks `$parentRunId` and calls `failSuspendedRun` on each suspended ancestor;
- **delegation** (the parent resumed first, the child resumed with `skipBubble === true`): the parent frame sees `!childRes.success` with no retryable code and calls `failSuspendedRun` on itself.

`failSuspendedRun` was `forgetSuspendedRun(run, 'failed')` plus a `failed` log record — it journalled **nothing**. So the leaf was restorable while every ancestor was recorded `failed` with its pause consumed and no snapshot (`restoreConsumedSuspension(PARENT)` answered `NO_CONSUMED_SUSPENSION`), and restoring the leaf completed it into a parent that never continues: `bubbleToParent` finds no parent suspension and logs. **The operator ended up worse off than before using the exit, and that state had no name anywhere.**

## The direction, and it was already ruled

Direction **①** — journal each consumed ancestor too, re-arm leaf-first — is #13937's shape 4 applied to a nested run (director seat, decision batch #21, comment 5491060439, maintainer verbatim 「其他同意」):

> 1. **shape 4**:`resumeInternal` 的消费顺序**不动**(崩溃跨越 exactly-once 保住);新增**显式运维动词**,把 terminally-failed 的 run 重新武装/重试 —— 「进得去出不来」的状态变成能离开的。
> 3. **shape 2 仅在与保住 exactly-once 的持久 claim/lease 同批设计时重开** —— 单独的顺序翻转 ⛔ **不做**(静默双跑替换可见失败,方向性错误);届时 `assertRunResumable` 的翻转必须同批钉住。

Direction ② — do not fail ancestors while a descendant is repairable — is a resume-ordering change, closed by point 3. It is **not implemented and not proposed here**. The consumption order in `resumeInternal` is byte-for-byte unchanged.

## What this does

1. **`failSuspendedRun` journals the pause it consumes**, from the same single producer (`journalConsumedSuspension`) and onto the same durable terminal row (the third argument to `recordLog`) as the strand's own snapshot — so a chain is repairable from any replica and after a restart, not only from the process that stranded it. The snapshot is taken before `forgetSuspendedRun`, from a `run` no traversal has touched, which is why there is no `cloneVariablesAtPause` here: the #15660 aliasing hazard is a failed attempt writing through a shared scope object, and no attempt has run against this run.

2. **Journalling is EARNED, not applied to every cascade.** An ancestor's pause is journalled exactly when the descendant whose failure consumed it is itself repairable — asked of the journal, not of the child's `status`, which is what makes a chain deeper than two levels re-armable by induction. A cascade from a descendant that is beyond repair still journals nothing: re-arming that ancestor would promise a chain repair that cannot be completed.

3. **`restoreConsumedSuspension` repairs the chain as one unit.** It resolves the chain read-only — down to the stranded descendant through the `subflow:`/`map:` correlation the engine already writes, up through `$parentRunId` — and re-arms every member **deepest first**, so an ancestor becomes resumable only after the run it is parked awaiting is parked again. Naming any member repairs all of it; the continuation is then re-issued once, on the run that was named.

4. **Per-run idempotence and the #14333 claim.** Every member goes through the same per-run call as a flat restore: its own in-process `restoring` claim, its own strict live-suspension read, its own two-witness read, its own durable park. A second restore finds every member parked, resolves an empty chain and answers `RUN_SUSPENDED` for the named run alone, minting no second pause anywhere.

5. **A chain hop the store cannot read is REPORTED**, at `warn`, naming the run and that the walk stopped there — a chain silently truncated by an outage would read to an operator as a complete repair.

### ⛔ What it deliberately does not do

**No ancestor is stamped `'stranded'`.** That word is the resume result of a run that consumed its OWN pause and then threw downstream, and nothing re-arms an ancestor by resuming it. A parent falsely marked `stranded` makes an operator retry a recovery that can never succeed, and every attempt reads as 「还没修好」 rather than 「这条路不存在」. The delegation path's return is untouched and still carries no status at all; that absence is pinned in both suites.

**No new marker on the journal, hot or durable.** The chain is resolved from links the engine already persists. A durable marker would be a store change; a hot-only one would make a chain resolvable in the process that stranded it and not in the replica that has to repair it after a restart — the one place this has to work.

## `packages/spec` — the red line, and why it is not crossed

`restoreConsumedSuspension` is declared at `packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts:828` as an optional member of `IAutomationService`. **Nothing under `packages/spec/**` is touched by this PR**, and the contract does not need to move, because that docblock already rules the case:

> **The result is deliberately NARROWER than the implementation's.** The engine answers its own wider `SuspensionRestoreResult` … That type lives with the engine and is not moved here (#16495, route (i)): `refusal` is typed as the string the implementation answers, not as an enumeration this contract would have to keep in step, and the wider type satisfies this one under `implements`.

The wider engine-owned result grew one optional key; the contract's four fields are unchanged and the wider type still satisfies the narrower one (`tsc --noEmit` green in both packages). The HTTP door in `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts` builds `{ runId, restored, reason }` explicitly rather than spreading the result, so the wire payload is byte-identical.

I also re-measured the seat's own correction, on `origin/main` at `bea76c928`, by declaration site rather than filename hit — it holds: the contract slot is in `packages/spec`, the implementation is `AutomationEngine` in `service-automation` (where the card's title says), and `plugin-approvals` carries prose references only. `git grep -ln` over `packages/` returns **28** files.

## Clause-② — both limbs measured

**Limb A — does it widen the accept set? YES.** The verb now acts on a class of runs it previously refused: a cascade-failed ancestor answered `NO_CONSUMED_SUSPENSION` and now answers `restored: true`. That is a widening of the input set the verb accepts, not a narrowing.

**Limb B — does it add or change a public surface? YES.** One new exported symbol, `ChainRestoreEntry`, and one new optional key on a published payload, `SuspensionRestoreResult.chain`, both from `@objectstack/service-automation`. Under the standing floor, a new exported symbol or a new key on a published payload is always `yes`.

Both limbs yes, so the claim-time declaration stands and `needs:contract-review` rides with this PR.

## Reproduction, RED first, on the committed tree

`packages/services/service-automation/src/nested-strand-chain-restore.test.ts` drives a real engine over a real store: a parent parked at a `subflow` node, a child parked at a pausing node whose downstream node throws. Committed as `ba926f716` and run on that commit:

```
Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  6 failed | 1 passed (7)
os-verify-lock: VERDICT command-exit 1
```

with the defect stated in the failures verbatim — `the ancestor now has a snapshot to put back: expected false to be true`, and `leaf-first, the whole chain in one call: expected undefined to deeply equal [ …(2) ]`. The one test that PASSES on the unfixed tree is the control: a cascade from a descendant that is not repairable already answered `NO_CONSUMED_SUSPENSION` correctly, and still must.

## Ablation — the direction OBSERVED, not the one predicted

Committed fix mutated in place (the ancestor journal deleted, every other line of the fix left standing), proven on disk before the run:

```
PRE   hash=7f77362b8733e494107e2f31ca809c73a54d6cba head=7f77362b8733e494107e2f31ca809c73a54d6cba occurrences=1
POST  hash=6546eb864a794f5a48c29fff7d0e51e803a8ba0f occurrences=0 injected x1
ablation-dist-preflight --absent: ✓ dist/: marker absent from all 6 built files
ABLATED service-automation pins exit=1   Tests  6 failed | 1 passed (7)
ABLATED plugin-approvals pins  exit=1   Tests  4 failed | 2 passed (6)
```

Direction observed: RED, as predicted, in both packages — and the service-automation leg reproduces the RED commit's shape exactly (6 red, the control still green). The `plugin-approvals` leg resolves the engine through `exports` into `dist/`, so the package was rebuilt between mutation and run and the marker's absence from `dist/` was proven before the colour was read.

Restore proven **by state**, not by exit code — whole-tree, because the build writes artifacts a per-path diff cannot see:

```
$ git status --porcelain      (empty)
$ git diff HEAD --stat        (empty)
$ git hash-object packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts
7f77362b8733e494107e2f31ca809c73a54d6cba
$ git rev-parse HEAD:packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts
7f77362b8733e494107e2f31ca809c73a54d6cba
```

`dist/` was then rebuilt and `ablation-dist-preflight` (present form) confirmed the marker is back in 2 built files, so nothing of the ablation survives into any later run.

## Why `plugin-approvals` is in this diff

Three pins in `stranded-run-repairability.test.ts` encoded the defect as the expected behaviour — `['cascade-failed ancestor', 'unrepairable']`, `refusal: 'NO_CONSUMED_SUSPENSION'` for the parent, and a positive control asserting the split. They are rewritten to hold the new truth **and to earn it**: PIN 1 now proves the shared label by showing that ONE call repairs both runs, so a regression that stops journalling the ancestor fails it even if somebody relabels the assertion. A new PIN 2b holds the either-end property.

Six docblocks in `approval-service.ts` documented the old limitation in prose ("no verb re-arms it", "#15222's cascade-failed ancestor is refused by that verb"). This change makes them false, so they are corrected. **No plugin logic changed** — `inspectStrandedRequests` asks the engine per run and the engine now answers differently. The `'unrepairable'` label is not dead: it keeps its other causes and its own drives in `stranded-request-inspection.test.ts`.

`approval-service.ts` is a known contention point in this lane, so the obligation is stated rather than the convenience. **What obliges it:** six passages in that file document the ENGINE's behaviour as a limitation of the plugin's own report — "so no verb re-arms it (#15222's shape)", "an `unrepairable` one (#15222's cascade-failed ancestor) is refused by that verb", "`restoreConsumedSuspension` refuses it". This PR makes each of those statements **false**, in the direction that matters: they tell the next author that a whole class of rows is beyond repair, when the verb now repairs it. Leaving them is not a smaller diff, it is a diff that ships a correct engine behind documentation that denies it — and that text ships, because these are docblocks on exported members and land in `dist/index.d.ts`. The edit is therefore **docblock-only, zero logic lines**, confined to the six passages this change falsifies, and the file was measured free of every open PR at claim time (19:12Z) and again at PR time, with a firing control on both zeros.

## Verification

| what | result |
|:--|:--|
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation test` | 130 files / **1546 passed**, exit 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals test` | 43 files / **730 passed**, exit 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals typecheck` | exit 0 (both `tsc --noEmit` and both `check:test-typecheck` ledgers unchanged) |
| import-side pins on the changed public face (`runtime` run-lifecycle door, `spec` contract, `verify` stranded details) | 55 passed, exit 0 |
| derived gates (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`) | **92 derived, 92 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN**, every one exit 0, reconciled with `--ran` carrying each exit code |
| `pnpm lint` (repo-wide, `eslint . --no-inline-config`) | **exit 0** at the final head `09bd86c1f` — the whole population, so no narrowing was claimed |

The gate set was re-derived after the docs commit, which pulled in 29 further families (63 to 92); all 92 were run on the final tree. Five readings were **NOT MEASURED** on their first attempt and are recorded as such, never rounded up: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:i18n` and `check:type-check-debt` answered **exit 3 = PREREQUISITE NOT MET** with the repo-wide `dist/` absent, and `check:lean-entry-closure` exit 1 was read against a tree being rebuilt concurrently — all cleared by a full `pnpm build` (73 tasks, exit 0). `check:type-check-debt` then answered exit 3 a second time under `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096`: the gate's own text says that cap is *tighter* than the 4144 MB its tsc needs and that it refuses to record 0 rather than guess, so it was re-run without the cap — the one place a heap ceiling was deliberately not applied, with the gate's own sentence as the reason. Exit 0.

Every heavy run went through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` with a stable `OS_VERIFY_LOCK_SLOT`.

## Docs — the drift check answered, and one page edited

The `docs-drift-check` bot's five hand-written rows are answered row by row in a PR comment, on the tree it named (`1ee43983c`, the merge of head into base), with the collisions named: **three are pure false positives** (a *cluster* `nodeId`, a *job-name* `flowName` placeholder, REST path parameters), one is a collision on a page that is nonetheless adjacent, and one — `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` — is real.

That page is **edited** here, in two places that were true-but-incomplete about exactly this change: the `restore-suspension` route row described re-arming the stranded run only, and the subflow section's «A child that fails terminally after the pause fails every waiting ancestor» is the sentence an operator reads to conclude the ancestors are unreachable. Both now state what the verb does for a chain, including that an ancestor is never stamped `stranded` and that an unrepairable descendant records no ancestor snapshot.

⭐ The second of those was found by the **emitter-blind hand search** the bot says it can never do — it states the rule by its inputs (a child, waiting ancestors) and shares no identifier with the diff. The search and its firing control are in the comment.

⛔ The four release-owned pages were read and none is wrong, so none is touched. `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx` — which the bot did **not** list — is called out there: its «tells a repairable strand from a cascade-failed run» is accurate as history for 17.4.0 and must stay.

## Acceptance notes

- **FILED as #17541 — the resume door under-reports `repairable` on the delegation exit.** The one thing this PR genuinely falsifies: `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts:1416` computes `repairable: status === 'stranded'`, the delegation frame stamps no status, and the verb now re-arms that run anyway — so the wire says `repairable: false` about a run the operator verb repairs, and `ResumeFailureDetailsSchema.repairable`'s own `.describe()` (`packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.ts:447`) states the opposite reason («promising a repair verb that will refuse is worse than promising nothing»). ⛔ Not fixed here: both candidate repairs move `packages/spec` — declaring `inspectConsumedSuspension` on `IAutomationService` (measured absent) or naming the condition in `AutomationResult.status` (and ⛔ never as `'stranded'`). Stopped and reported, as the red line requires. The reproduction is already committed here (the `DELEGATION` test); only the delegation exit is affected.
- **Noted, not filed — the operator door cannot see the chain.** `POST /automation/runs/:runId/restore` answers `{ runId, restored, reason }`; the `chain` this verb now returns is in-process only. That is the contract's declared narrowing, and its own docblock names the remedy ("A second consumer that needs the vocabulary itself is a spec card, never a widening at a call site"). Successor if it is ever wanted: the `domain:spec` seat. Not a defect — the repair works through the door unchanged, the operator simply does not see the chain listed.
- **Noted, not filed — a cascade from an unrepairable descendant leaves that descendant's own pause live.** With the child's flow unregistered, its resume answers `RUN_NOT_FOUND` without consuming its pause, and the parent frame then fails the parent while the child stays parked. The synthetic route to it (deregistering a flow under a parked run) is not a real deployment shape and I have no repro that is one, so this is an observation rather than a card. Successor: none identified today.
